
```{r cmp-calc, include = FALSE}
# Shared by the example vignettes. Needs: fit, time, ref (mixsiar_reference()), blocks
# (diet blocks to plot), and optionally ref_raw (MixSIAR fitted to the raw source data).
cmp <- compare_mixsiar(fit, ref$draws, ref$summary)
diet <- cmp[!is.na(cmp$w1), ]
gaps <- abs(diet$pfn_mean - diet$mixsiar_mean)
worst <- diet[which.max(gaps), ]
speedup <- ref$info$minutes * 60 / time[["elapsed"]]
has_raw <- exists("ref_raw") && !is.null(ref_raw)
```

MixSIAR `r if (ok) ref$info$mixsiar` fitted the same model to the same data with
`r if (ok) ref$info$chains` chains of `r if (ok) format(ref$info$chain_length, big.mark = ",")`
iterations (burn-in `r if (ok) format(ref$info$burn, big.mark = ",")`, MixSIAR's "long"
run), which took `r num(ref$info$minutes, 0)` minutes (largest Gelman-Rubin diagnostic
`r num(ref$info$max_psrf, 3)`). MixSIARPFN took `r num(time[["elapsed"]], 1)` seconds,
about `r if (ok) format(signif(speedup, 2), big.mark = ",")` times faster.

Means, SDs, 95% intervals and the Wasserstein-1 distance between the two posteriors
(W1: how far, on average, one posterior's mass has to move to match the other, on the
proportion scale):

```{r cmp-table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = cmp$name,
  `MixSIARPFN mean` = round(cmp$pfn_mean, 3), `MixSIAR mean` = round(cmp$mixsiar_mean, 3),
  `MixSIARPFN SD` = round(cmp$pfn_sd, 3), `MixSIAR SD` = round(cmp$mixsiar_sd, 3),
  `MixSIARPFN 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", cmp$pfn_q2.5, cmp$pfn_q97.5),
  `MixSIAR 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", cmp$mixsiar_q2.5, cmp$mixsiar_q97.5),
  W1 = round(cmp$w1, 3), check.names = FALSE))
```

```{r cmp-density, fig.height = 4.5}
for (b in blocks) print(plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, block = b))
```

```{r cmp-means, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_compare(fit, ref$draws, type = "means")
```

**What this shows.** MixSIARPFN's diet proportions differ from MixSIAR's by
`r num(mean(gaps), 3)` on average (MixSIAR's posterior SDs are about
`r num(mean(diet$mixsiar_sd))`), the mean W1 between the two posteriors is
`r num(mean(diet$w1), 3)`, and the median ratio of their SDs is
`r num(median(diet$sd_ratio))`. The largest difference in a posterior mean is for
`r if (ok) worst$name` (`r num(worst$pfn_mean, 3)` against `r num(worst$mixsiar_mean, 3)`).

```{r cmp-raw, include = FALSE, eval = ok && has_raw}
raw_cmp <- merge(
  aggregate(value ~ name, ref_raw$draws, mean),
  aggregate(value ~ name, ref$draws, mean), by = "name", suffixes = c("_raw", "_means"))
raw_gap <- mean(abs(raw_cmp$value_raw - raw_cmp$value_means))
```

`r if (ok && has_raw) paste0("The source data here are raw samples, which MixSIARPFN summarises to each source's mean, SD and sample size. MixSIAR's own example fits the raw samples instead, estimating each source's mean and variance in the model. That MixSIAR fit (", round(ref_raw$info$minutes), " minutes, largest Gelman-Rubin diagnostic ", format(round(ref_raw$info$max_psrf, 3), nsmall = 3), if (ref_raw$info$max_psrf > 1.1) ", so not fully converged" else "", ") and MixSIAR's fit to the summaries differ by ", format(round(raw_gap, 3), nsmall = 3), " in posterior means on average, so summarising the sources changes little here, and the comparison above is like for like: both methods fitted the same summaries.")`
